narrator.instruct: Gripping, energetic storyteller telling a comic royal fable with a twist, brisk and excited, never calm.

shah.instruct: Booming, spoiled Persian king at his own victory feast, loud, demanding and full of himself.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The Shah keeps adding drummers, and every drum makes his feast more boring.

lines.speaker: shah
lines.text: Louder! This music must never stop!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: It's his victory feast. The first song sent his joy needle to the top.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Out in the yard, a blacksmith hammers a plain iron ring.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: But hours later, the same music barely moves the needle.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: So he orders more musicians, then a bigger drum, then one the size of a cart.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: It rolls off the stage and flattens the flute player.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The blacksmith offers his ring. It reads: this too shall pass.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He hurls the ring. It snaps a lute string, and the whole hall goes silent.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Then the music starts again, and the needle shoots past the top.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You see, in two thousand nine, researchers tested TV shows with and without ad breaks.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: People said they'd rather skip the breaks. But breaks made the shows more fun.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Joy fades as you get used to it, a spring dragging the needle down.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A break cuts the spring, and the needle jumps back up.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: It fails for people who barely get used to anything.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: So now the Shah stops his own band every hour, with a gong.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: And your favorite show? It just cut to an ad.
